summary: Practise conflict-sensitive indicators, outcome evidence and peacebuilding reports. Explore the five-day foundation course and apply MERL at work.
lede: Monitoring, evaluation, reporting and learning (MERL) in peacebuilding helps programme teams assess change while accounting for conflict dynamics. It is designed for programme officers, monitoring specialists and peacebuilding team leads who need to track results and use evidence to adapt delivery. Participants practise mapping a theory of change, selecting conflict-sensitive indicators, checking data quality and turning findings into reports and learning actions.
audienceIntro: This foundation course is designed for professionals whose routine responsibilities include documenting peacebuilding activity, checking whether programme results reflect conflict dynamics, or using evidence to adjust delivery. It suits new MERL practitioners and staff who contribute data or programme decisions without requiring prior specialist training.
modules: Do No Harm and Conflict Sensitivity
Theory of Change and Peacebuilding Results
Most Significant Change and Learning Reviews
Peacebuilding MERL Reporting and Action Plans
prerequisites: Foundation level. Prior MERL training is not required; familiarity with programme delivery, community engagement or peacebuilding work is useful. No coding is required. Bring a laptop with Excel installed or accessible for the indicator-tracking exercise; no additional software installation is needed.
